Asa Gray (in Ann. Lyceum Nat. Hist. New York 4: 106. 1837) mentioned that the genera Disporum Salisb., Drapiezia Blume, Schelhammera R.Br., Tricyrtis Wall., and Uvularia L. seemed to constitute a small section of the family Liliaceae. He did not coin any infrafamilial name based on the stem of the genus name Uvularia.  Endlicher (1840) published 'Subtribus Uvularieae [A.Gray] and mentioned 'Ex sententia cl. Gray Liliaceis adsertbendae'. Subsequently, Meisner (1842: 306) published 'Tribus  Uvularieae Asa Gray; Kunth (Jul 1843) published 'Uvularieae A. Gray at the rank of family; and Torrey (late 1843) published 'Suborder Uvularieae A. Gray; Kunth' at the rank of subfamily.  Since it is not logical to associate Asa Gray's name with the 4 infrafamilial names at different ranks, the authorship A. Gray ex is associated only for the first published name, subtrib. Uvulariinae.
